text:
maria.sr-sales: FYI — ACME execs sign this week, asking for a committed plan. They quoted 10M tokens/day steady, with 100 RPS peaks for 30m spikes, and ~5k concurrent chat sessions during business hours. Need: reserved GPU sizing, autoscale rules, preheat/runbook, and short answers for their security questionnaire. Can eng + security confirm feasibility and a proposal by EOD Friday?

raj.solutions: Quick clarifying q's — which model family are they expecting to run (L/XL), avg prompt+resp token length, and mix chat vs batch embedding traffic?

maria.sr-sales: They want a default of an open 16B class (quantized) for chat, avg 350 tokens per request (prompt+response), and ~15% of calls are embeddings (short). Traffic profile: steady baseline ~1.3k RPS distributed, spikes to 100 RPS for 30m (this is per-region, primarily us-west & eu-west).

jesse.infra: Rough math: 10M tokens/day -> ~116 tokens/sec avg. But their RPS/seq length yields peak token throughput. For a quantized 16B on A10-ish perf, estimate ~10–12 reqs/sec per GPU at 350 tokens with KV cache cold; with prefix caching that improves. I'd propose: reserved pool of 6 GPUs per region for steady throughput, with burst reserve to shared pool (auto-burst) of +4 GPUs for spikes. That gives headroom and keeps latency SLOs.

olivia.security: Security checklist items we'll need for the questionnaire: VPC peering options, KMS key for logs, SIEM ingestion, retention windows, and SOC2 attestation copy. I can draft short answers but need confirmation on whether customer requires HSM-backed keys.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: preheat-job/acme-commit-241900 — estimated duration 45m (KV warmup).

raj.solutions: Pricing note — committed discount request of ~30% vs on-demand. With reserved GPUs the unit cost drops ~28–35% depending on term & burst allowances. If we include burst credits and autoscale overrides the effective discount changes; we should model a 12/24/36 month commit and show cost/throughput curves.

maria.sr-sales: Can someone sketch the autoscale policy we plan to propose? They want deterministic behavior during spikes (no cold-start latency >200ms 95p).

jesse.infra: Proposed autoscale snippet (pseudo-config):
```
autoscale: 
  min_reserved: 6
  max_total: 10
  scale_up_policy: 
    trigger: queue_latency_ms > 50 OR cpu_util > 75% for 15s
    add: 1 gpu (cooldown 30s)
  scale_down_policy:
    trigger: cpu_util < 30% for 120s
    remove: 1 gpu (cooldown 60s)
  preheat_on_schedule:
    - region: us-west
      window: "08:30-09:00"
    - region: eu-west
      window: "07:30-08:00"
  burst_strategy: allow_shared_burst (max 4 gpus, fairness=prefer-dedicated)
```
This keeps 6 reserved hot, allows fast +1 increments, and uses shared burst for larger surges. KV cache warmup job is mandatory before big spikes; preheat windows above.

olivia.security: For the questionnaire answers: we can confirm VPC peering, KMS (customer-managed ok), we've got audit logs with 90-day retention by default (expandable), and SOC2 + ISO docs available. If they want HSM, that's an add-on. I'll draft language and ping legal for any NDA specifics.

raj.solutions: Operational notes: recommend canary rollout for model versions (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant on overload. Also recommend prefix/KV caching keys be customer-specific to avoid cross-tenant pollution.

maria.sr-sales: Perfect — action items for EOD Friday: (1) jesse: finalize GPU count + expected p95 latency numbers for proposed config, (2) raj: cost comparisons 12/24/36mo incl burst credits, (3) olivia: draft questionnaire answers + list of docs to attach. I'll consolidate and send to ACME.

jesse.infra: Will do. Quick estimate p95: with reserved 6 + burst plan, p95 latency ~180ms across typical chat flows (quantized 16B, KV warm). If we remove preheat, expect p95 ~320ms on cold-cache.

maria.sr-sales: thanks all — I'll book a 30m sync with ACME Friday afternoon and share this thread. @olivia.security if you can attach SOC2 and the KMS/HSM note that helps the sign-off. :thumbsup:

olivia.security: On it. I'll attach docs and the draft answers before EOD.

raj.solutions: I'll drop a spreadsheet with cost rows + a short one-pager on autoscale tradeoffs by lunchtime.

maria.sr-sales: Awesome — closing loop.
